Command: Perform chalitzah if the brother refuses levirate marriage
Summary: One of the family laws of Deuteronomy 21–25: perform chalitzah if the brother refuses levirate marriage. These laws protected the weaker party at each family step.
Commandment: Perform chalitzah if the brother refuses levirate marriage
Application: These civil provisions belonged to ancient Israel's family law and have passed with it; the protection of the weaker party they aimed at remains the lesson.
Purpose: To release the widow publicly and honourably when the brother refuses levirate duty: the shoe-loosening ceremony frees her to marry another (Deuteronomy 25:9-10).
Function: One of the family laws of Deuteronomy 21–25: perform chalitzah if the brother refuses levirate marriage. A moral law in its traditional classing: it addressed character and conduct within Israel. What it wanted was to release the widow publicly and honourably when the brother refuses levirate duty: the shoe-loosening ceremony frees her to marry another. The answer was practical, not abstract. These civil provisions belonged to ancient Israel's family law and have passed with it.
